questions.question: What happens to the projected 2D position of a 3D point as its depth Z increases (moves further from camera)?
options: It moves further from the image center
It moves closer to the image center
It stays at the same position
questions.explanation: From the perspective projection equation x = f·X/Z, as Z increases, the projected position x shrinks toward zero (the center). This is perspective foreshortening — why railroad tracks appear to converge.

questions.question: In NeRF, why do we use INVERSE projection (2D → 3D rays) instead of forward projection (3D → 2D)?
options: Because we need to shoot rays into the scene to query the neural network at 3D points
Because the intrinsic matrix K is not invertible
questions.explanation: NeRF's neural network lives in 3D space. For each pixel, we must generate a ray and sample 3D points along it to query the MLP for density and color. This requires going from 2D pixels back to 3D rays.
